evidence.reference_title: Recurrent internal tandem duplications of BCOR in clear cell sarcoma of the kidney.
evidence.snippet: Here we report on the identification of somatic internal tandem duplications (ITDs) clustering in the C terminus of BCOR in 23 of 27 (85%) pediatric clear cell sarcomas of the kidney (CCSK) from two independent cohorts. We profile CCSK tumours using a combination of whole-exome, transcriptome and targeted sequencing. Identical ITD mutations are found in primary and relapsed tumour pairs but not in adjacent normal kidney or blood. Mutant BCOR transcripts and proteins are markedly upregulated in ITD-positive tumours.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical relevance of BCOR internal tandem duplication and TP53 aberration in clear cell sarcoma of the kidney.
evidence.snippet: BCOR ITD, YWHAE rearrangement, BCOR-CCNB3 fusion and TP53 status were examined by polymerase chain reaction, fluorescence in situ hybridization, or Sanger sequencing in a cohort of 39 patients with CCSK. Among them, 34 cases (87.18%) had BCOR ITD, 1 (2.56%) had YWHAE rearrangement, and 1 (2.56%) had BCOR-CCNB3 gene fusion. The remaining 3 (7.69%) harbored none of these aberrations. BCOR ITD, YWHAE rearrangement and BCOR-CCNB3 were mutually exclusive.

nodes.description: The recurrent lesion of CCSK: a somatic internal tandem duplication (ITD) clustering in the C terminus of BCOR, within the sequence encoding the PUFD domain, which is important for forming the variant polycomb repressive complex 1 and through which BCOR binds PCGF1 in that complex. BCOR can act as a transcriptional corepressor: it interacts selectively with the POZ domain of BCL-6 and can potentiate BCL-6 repression. Somatic ITDs were found in 23 of 27 paediatric CCSKs (85%) from two independent cohorts, identical in primary and relapsed tumour pairs and absent from adjacent normal kidney and blood, and mutant BCOR transcripts and proteins were markedly upregulated in ITD-positive tumours. In another series the ITD was found in all 20 CCSKs and in none of 193 other paediatric renal tumours, and these CCSKs expressed only an aberrant BCOR allele, which the authors read as a close correlation between the BCOR aberration and CCSK tumorigenesis. Expression profiling of patient tumours suggested that CCSK arises within a renal mesenchymal cell, a later study suggested a primitive mesodermal cell able to differentiate towards both nephrons and stroma, and the cell of origin is not established.

evidence.reference_title: Consistent in-frame internal tandem duplications of BCOR characterize clear cell sarcoma of the kidney.
evidence.snippet: We identified internal tandem duplications in the BCOR gene (BCL6 corepressor) affecting the C terminus in 100% (20/20) of CCSK tumors but in none (0/193) of the other pediatric renal tumors. CCSK tumors expressed only an aberrant BCOR allele, indicating a close correlation between BCOR aberration and CCSK tumorigenesis.

evidence.reference_title: Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney demonstrates an embryonic signature indicative of a primitive nephrogenic origin.
evidence.snippet: As this marker discriminates the intermediate mesoderm from other mesodermal structures, our study could suggest that CCSK arises from a mesodermal cell type that retains the capacity to initiate differentiation towards both nephrons and stroma, but remains locked in a primitive state.

nodes.description: High-dose chemotherapy followed by autologous bone marrow transplantation (ABMT) for relapsed disease. In the combined SIOP and AIEOP series it was given to 14 of 37 relapsed patients after chemotherapy, surgery and/or radiotherapy. Among the patients who completed the intended relapse treatment it was given to 13 of the 21 who reached a second complete remission and to 1 of the 7 who did not, a comparison the authors say their numbers do not allow them to test statistically. They conclude that intensive treatment aiming for local control, followed by high-dose chemotherapy and ABMT, seems to be of benefit to enhance survival. Summarising their series and earlier reports, 12 of 24 relapsed patients so treated were alive without disease after a median follow-up of 52 months, but the authors caution that the treatment is mostly given to patients who have already reached a second complete remission and that it carries direct and late toxicity. No standard treatment guidelines are available for relapsed CCSK, because too few relapsed patients have been reported to establish the contribution of each treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment and outcome of patients with relapsed clear cell sarcoma of the kidney: a combined SIOP and AIEOP study.
evidence.snippet: Summarising our study and previous reports, in total 24 relapsed CCSK patients received high-dose chemotherapy followed by ABMT, of which 12 patients (50%) were alive without disease after a median follow-up of 52 months (range, 9–103 months) ... This seems to be promising, although it should be emphasised that this high-dose chemotherapy is mostly applied in a selected group of patients who already achieved a second CR. In addition, high-dose chemotherapy followed by ABMT may cause treatment-related direct and late toxicity and needs to be weighed against the risk of disease-related mortality

nodes.description: Chemotherapy for relapse after complete remission. In a combined SIOP and AIEOP series, 30 of 37 relapsed patients received chemotherapy in different combinations, 19 had surgical excision and 18 radiotherapy, and 14 went on to high-dose chemotherapy with autologous bone marrow transplantation; 22 of the 37 reached a second complete remission, 15 of whom relapsed again. Five of the 13 patients with an isolated brain relapse received ICE (ifosfamide, carboplatin and etoposide), and three of them achieved a long-term complete response, which the authors read as possibly promising for brain relapse while noting that they have no data on the influence of upfront treatment; one patient died of septic shock after one cycle of ICE. The agents and regimen bound here are those of ICE, one of the combinations used. No standard treatment guideline was available for relapsed CCSK except in the United Kingdom, and the authors state that too few relapsed patients have been reported to establish the contributions of chemotherapy, high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell transplantation, radiotherapy and surgery, so no standard treatment guidelines are available for this patient group.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment and outcome of patients with relapsed clear cell sarcoma of the kidney: a combined SIOP and AIEOP study.
evidence.snippet: No standard treatment guideline was available for relapsed CCSK, except in the United Kingdom where relapsed patients were treated according to the recommendations of the UKWR trial including carboplatin, etoposide and cyclophosphamide followed by high-dose melphalan (Hale et al, 2008) (Supplementary Table 3). ... Thirty out of thirty-seven patients (81%) were treated with different combinations of chemotherapy, in 19/37 patients (51%) surgical excision was performed (after biopsy confirming CCSK), 18/37 patients (49%) were treated with radiotherapy (median radiotherapy dose 27 Gy, range, 12–32 Gy) and 14/37 patients (38%) received subsequently high-dose chemotherapy and autologous bone marrow transplantation (ABMT)

evidence.reference_title: Treatment and outcome of patients with relapsed clear cell sarcoma of the kidney: a combined SIOP and AIEOP study.
evidence.snippet: In our series, 5 out of 13 patients with an isolated relapse in the brain were treated with ICE chemotherapy, of which three patients achieved a long-term complete response. This may indicate that treatment including ICE is promising for patients with a relapse in the brain, although we currently have no data on the influence of other factors like type of upfront treatment and hence, development of resistance.

nodes.description: The alternative recurrent lesion: t(10;17)(q22;p13), with breakpoints mapped to 17p13.3 and 10q22.3 in an index tumour, rearranges YWHAE and FAM22 into an in-frame YWHAE-FAM22 fusion transcript joining exons 1-5 of YWHAE to exons 2-7 of FAM22; the FAM22 members involved include FAM22B and FAM22E, now NUTM2B and NUTM2E. The transcript was detected in 6 of 50 further CCSKs tested (12% in that cohort). In a cohort of 159 CCSKs the BCOR internal tandem duplication and the YWHAE fusion were mutually exclusive, and 11.8% of tumours carried neither when tested by those assays. In a 39-patient cohort tested by PCR, FISH or Sanger sequencing, a YWHAE rearrangement (1 tumour), BCOR ITD (34) and BCOR::CCNB3 fusion (1) were mutually exclusive, and 3 tumours had none of them detected.

evidence.reference_title: Characterization of the chromosomal translocation t(10;17)(q22;p13) in clear cell sarcoma of kidney.
evidence.snippet: Using fluorescently labelled bacterial artificial chromosomes (BACs) and a chromosome-walking strategy on an index case of CCSK with t(10;17)(q22;p13) by karyotype, we identified the chromosomal breakpoints on 17p13.3 and 10q22.3. The translocation results in rearrangement of YWHAE on chromosome 17 and FAM22 on chromosome 10, producing an in-frame fusion transcript of ~3 kb, incorporating exons 1-5 of YWHAE and exons 2-7 of FAM22, as determined by RT-PCR using YWHAE- and FAM22-specific primers. The YWHAE-FAM22 transcript was detected in six of 50 further CCSKs tested, therefore showing an overall incidence of 12% in our cohort. ... Based on the chromosome 10 breakpoint identified by FISH and the sequences of the full-length transcripts obtained, the FAM22 members involved in the translocation in these CCSK cases include FAM22B and FAM22E.

evidence.reference_title: Mutually exclusive BCOR internal tandem duplications and YWHAE-NUTM2 fusions in clear cell sarcoma of kidney: not the full story.
evidence.snippet: We analysed a cohort of 159 CCSKs and can now not only confirm that there is indeed mutual exclusivity of these BCOR and YWHAE mutations, but also show that a substantial proportion (in this series 11.8%) of CCSKs bear neither mutation when tested by these assays, raising the possibility of distinct aetiologies for subsets of CCSK.
